notes.summary: Constructs the genuine ordinary model, proves every admissibility antecedent and its degenerate reference residual, and constructs the fixed-pole solution for continuous factored densities on a background whose smooth positive perturbations are all non-Gauduchon.
notes.detailedSummary: For θ=(a+λ)ω₁+b(x)ω₂, the stated piecewise φ is exactly Pθ[ψ], is bounded-difference equivalent to ψ, and satisfies sup φ=0 and Pθ[φ]=φ. Its extended reference mass is positive finite, and its horizontal residual vanishes outside the cutoff disk. For every λ/(a+λ)<ε<1, ψ is an explicit competitor proving that Pεθ(φ) is genuine. The background is positive and big, with dd^c θ≠0. For continuous positive H satisfying q e^F/(2b)=H(x), a logarithmic Green kernel constructs a mean-zero bounded continuous w with dd^c w=(cH−a)ω₁. The genuine solution u=ψ+w has extended products Ω and Ω², where Ω=cHω₁+bω₂ is continuous uniformly positive. Only after these antecedents are established are the supplied scalar uniqueness and nonempty full-support results invoked.
notes.text:
This is an independent ordinary proof draft from the frozen statement-only input. All forms from the factors are pulled back to X=P¹_x×P¹_y. Write p={Z₀=0}, D=p×P¹_y, r=|z|² for z=Z₁/Z₀, K=a+λ, R=a/λ, and β=ω₁+ω₂. Mean zero on the first sphere uses ω₁, and mean zero on X uses dW=ω₁∧ω₂.

The normalization dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π) gives ω₁=dd^c log(1+r), ∫_{r<R}ω₁=R/(1+R), and dd^c ψ=λ[D]−λω₁. Since K>0 and b has a positive minimum, θ≥κβ for some κ>0. Thus θ is smooth positive, hence semipositive and big, already admitting the strictly positive current θ with potential zero. Likewise η=aω₁+bω₂ is positive. Consequently θ+dd^c ψ=η+λ[D] is positive, so ψ is genuine θ-psh.

For the claimed exterior formula φ=a log r+C*−K log(1+r), its value at R is zero because 1+R=K/λ. Its radial derivative is a/r−K/(1+r)=(a−λr)/(r(1+r)), which vanishes at R and is negative for r>R. The first derivatives match the zero interior function, so dd^c φ has no circle-supported term. Near p, with ξ=1/z, φ=λ log|ξ|²+C*−K log(1+|ξ|²). Therefore, setting α=K 1_{r<R}ω₁, with the circle irrelevant to this area density,

Kω₁+dd^c φ=α+λ[D], and θ+dd^c φ=α+bω₂+λ[D].

These formulas prove positivity. The displayed φ is continuous and C¹ off D, piecewise smooth, with its actual logarithmic limit −∞ on D. It is the genuine canonical representative. Its supremum is zero, and ∫α=KR/(1+R)=a.

For r≤R, φ−ψ=λ log(1+r). For r≥R, φ−ψ=a log(r/(1+r))+C*. The latter increases from λ log(1+R) at R to C*. Thus 0≤φ−ψ≤C* off D, and both functions have the same poles on D. In particular φ~ψ and C*>0.

Here is the envelope comparison. Suppose v is genuine θ-psh with v≤0 and v≤ψ+C. Restrict to each first-factor sphere with y fixed. Such a restriction is either identically −∞ or genuine Kω₁-psh. To justify the restricted inequality even for the nonclosed background, locally add a large smooth strictly psh correction, convolve on smaller coordinate balls, restrict the smooth inequalities, and pass to the canonical subharmonic restriction; the smooth horizontal background coefficients tend uniformly to those of Kω₁. On r>R, v−φ is subharmonic because dd^c φ=−Kω₁ there. It is bounded above near p by v≤ψ+C and φ~ψ, hence has a removable subharmonic singularity at p. Its boundary upper values on r=R are at most zero. The maximum principle on the resulting exterior disk gives v≤φ. On r≤R this already follows from v≤0. Identically −∞ slices also satisfy the conclusion.

Every competitor for Pθ(min(ψ+C,0)) therefore lies below φ, and its usc envelope remains below the usc function φ. For C≥C*, φ itself is a competitor. Thus these envelopes equal φ for all C≥C*, proving Pθ[ψ]=φ. For min(φ+C,0), C≥0, φ is a competitor, while every other competitor is bounded above by ψ+C+C*. The same comparison gives Pθ(min(φ+C,0))=φ, proving Pθ[φ]=φ.

The reference products can be constructed directly. The closed positive current T=Kω₁+dd^c φ is pulled back from the first curve. Its non-pluripolar first product is α, because the divisorial term is discarded. Its non-pluripolar square is zero: off D it is horizontal, including at the cutoff circle where φ is locally bounded and depends only on x. Its Bedford–Taylor products are pullbacks of products on a one-dimensional factor. Expanding with the task's smooth correction θ−Kω₁=bω₂ gives the extended first product α+bω₂ and MA_extθ(φ)=2bα∧ω₂. The reference mass is 2∫bα, between 2a min b and 2a max b, hence positive finite. The horizontal residual α vanishes on the nonempty open region r>R away from p.

For λ/K<ε<1, εθ+dd^c ψ=(εK−λ)ω₁+εbω₂+λ[D]≥0. Since ψ≤φ, ψ is a genuine competitor for Pεθ(φ). The upper envelope and its canonical regularization lie between ψ and φ. The usual local upper-envelope argument, after adding a smooth strictly psh correction, makes the regularization εθ-psh. The usc obstacle preserves the upper bound at every point, including D where it forces −∞. Thus the envelope is genuine, finite off D, and even of the same bounded-difference type. This proves existence for every required ε.

Also dd^c θ=dd^c_x b∧ω₂≠0: otherwise b would be harmonic on a compact connected sphere and therefore constant. On a complex surface a positive form Γ is Gauduchon exactly when dd^c Γ=0. For every smooth real v, dd^c(θ+dd^c v)=dd^c θ. Hence every smooth positive potential perturbation of θ is non-Gauduchon.

Now assume F∈C(X) and q e^F/(2b)=H(x), with H continuous strictly positive. Define m=∫Hω₁, c=a/m, A=cH, and f=A−a. Then A has a positive minimum and ∫Aω₁=a, so f is continuous real and mean zero.

Use the Green kernel G(x,s)=log d_ch(x,s)², with squared chordal distance on the sphere. Poincaré–Lelong gives dd^c_x G(·,s)=δ_s−ω₁. Rotational invariance, or the uniform distribution of squared chordal distance on [0,1], gives ∫G(x,s)ω₁(x)=−1 and ∫|G(x,s)|ω₁(s)=1. Define w(x)=∫G(x,s)f(s)ω₁(s). It is real, bounded by ||f||∞, and mean zero. It is continuous: the integral of |G| in a radius-r neighborhood of its singularity is bounded uniformly by C r²(1+|log r|); outside such neighborhoods the kernel is uniformly continuous. Splitting the integral first near the singularities and then on their complement proves continuity. Fubini against smooth tests yields dd^c w=fω₁. No derivative of H is required.

For later use, average A and w over rotations with smooth probability kernels supported in shrinking neighborhoods of the identity. The resulting smooth functions A_j,w_j⁰ satisfy A_j→A uniformly, A_j≥min A, ∫A_jω₁=a, w_j⁰→w uniformly, ∫w_j⁰ω₁=0, and dd^c w_j⁰=(A_j−a)ω₁. Smoothness follows from group convolution; commutation with dd^c follows from rotational invariance of ω₁.

Set u=ψ+w, with value −∞ on D. Then θ+dd^c u=λ[D]+Ω, where Ω=Aω₁+bω₂ is continuous strictly positive. The continuous representative off D and logarithmic limit on D make u genuine θ-psh, and boundedness of w gives u~ψ~φ. The closed horizontal current Kω₁+dd^c u=Aω₁+λ[D] has non-pluripolar first product Aω₁ and square zero. Expanding with bω₂ gives the actual extended products Ω and Ω²=2Ab dW. Alternatively, the preceding smoothing identifies the bounded-potential products off D through uniform residual tensor convergence; the resulting continuous densities give D zero mass, so their non-pluripolar extensions are precisely these forms. This product construction precedes any supporting probability.

Since 2Ab=c q e^F, MA_extθ(u)=c e^F dV.

Exact primary-premise judgment: the supplied admissible scalar-solvability/uniqueness and nonempty-full-support theorem is now applicable. X is compact connected of complex dimension two; dV is a smooth positive probability volume; θ is smooth semipositive big; φ is a genuine normalized ordinary model of positive finite mass; and genuine Pεθ(φ) exists for ε∈(0,1). Every continuous logarithmic density is bounded. Scalar uniqueness therefore identifies cφ(F)=c, and the permitted theorem supplies nonempty full supporting sets. No potential uniqueness or rough weighted-product theorem is invoked.

The frozen operative input and complete proof are retained in input.md and proof.md in /workspace/research/native-workers/codex-q8V07l.

notes.summary: Defines the weak linearized operator and weighted current before using supports, proves every full support is stationary, and proves stationary uniqueness for all finite signed measures. Consequently the full supporting set is a singleton and the normalized integrable weight is unique almost everywhere.
notes.detailedSummary: For the solution of n1, ρ=1/(2ab) gives the positive closed continuous current Q=ρΩ and normalized probability ν=ρΩ²=(A/a)dW. The derivative along every smooth signed potential perturbation is 2Ω∧dd^c h, with Lh=Δ₁h/A+Δ₂h/b. Exact density curves force every support on the full C(X) to annihilate L. A complete signed-measure uniqueness proof separates spherical harmonics in y, uses the logarithmic Green kernel to turn each finite measure into an L² density, and then applies a justified spectral energy test. It yields all finite signed annihilators as C A dW, so the sole invariant probability and full support is ν. Any normalized nonnegative integrable weight satisfying dd^c(ρ̃Ω)=0 equals ρ almost everywhere.
notes.text:
Retain n1's constructed solution, with continuous strictly positive Ω=Aω₁+bω₂, ∫Aω₁=a, and the verified admissible reference.

Define ρ=1/(2ab). It is smooth strictly positive. Multiplication by the continuous form Ω is ordinary coefficientwise multiplication, defined independently of supporting probabilities. Thus Q=ρΩ=(A/(2ab))ω₁+(1/(2a))ω₂ is a positive order-zero current. A horizontal two-form f(x)ω₁ is closed distributionally: its horizontal exterior derivative would have degree three on a real two-dimensional factor, and it has no y dependence. The second summand has constant coefficient. Therefore dQ=0 and dd^c Q=0. Moreover ρΩ²=(A/a)dW=:ν and ∫ρΩ²=(1/a)∫Aω₁=1.

Let h be any smooth real function on all X. For sufficiently small positive or negative t, Ω_t=Ω+t dd^c h remains continuous strictly positive and u+t h retains the exact logarithmic pole and ordinary type. Its extended products are Ω_t and Ω_t². To verify this for arbitrary mixed-factor h, smooth w as in n1 and add t h. On relatively compact sets outside D a common smooth closed local correction makes the potentials psh. Uniform convergence of these bounded potentials gives their Bedford–Taylor products, while uniform convergence of the residual tensor coefficients gives Ω_t². The resulting continuous densities have zero mass on D, so this is also the non-pluripolar extension.

The exact identity Ω_t²=Ω²+2t Ω∧dd^c h+t²(dd^c h)² proves D_u MA_ext(h)=2Ω∧dd^c h, with uniform-density remainder. The mixed Hessian blocks vanish when wedged with diagonal Ω. With dd^c_i h=(Δ_i h)ω_i, the corresponding logarithmic operator is L_u h=2Ω∧dd^c h/Ω²=Δ₁h/A+Δ₂h/b. It is linear and continuous C²(X)→C(X), hence continuous on smooth tests, and uniformly elliptic because A,b have positive minima. Integration over the factors gives ∫L_u h dν=(1/a)∫Δ₁h dW+(1/a)∫(A/b)Δ₂h dW=0.

Every full supporting probability annihilates L_u. Define F_t=log(Ω_t²/(c dV)). This is continuous and need not factor. Uniform determinant expansion gives F_t=F+t L_u h+O(t²) in sup norm. The actual solution u+t h has type φ and solves the equation with scalar c. The scalar uniqueness permitted after n1's antecedent verification gives Bφ(F_t)=Bφ(F)=log c. For σ∈Aφ(F), its inequality for every G∈C(X), applied to G=F_t, gives ∫(F_t−F)dσ≤0. Dividing for positive and negative t and passing to zero proves ∫L_u h dσ=0. Thus the argument applies to the full supporting set, rather than a restriction to factored densities.

Here is the entire finite-signed-measure uniqueness argument. On a single sphere define Δ by dd^c f=(Δf)ω. This smooth Laplacian is symmetric and nonpositive. Take an orthonormal real spherical harmonic basis e_k with Δe_k=−μ_k e_k, e_0=1, μ_0=0 and μ_k>0 for nonconstant harmonics, including multiplicities. Finite harmonic sums are uniformly dense in C(P¹): polynomial restrictions decompose into spherical harmonics, and Stone–Weierstrass applies. They are consequently complete in L²(ω).

First prove a scalar lemma. Let r be continuous strictly positive and ζ a finite signed measure satisfying ∫(Δf−μ r f)dζ=0 for all smooth f, with μ≥0. If μ=0, testing every harmonic makes all nonconstant coefficients vanish. Uniform harmonic density then gives ζ=ζ(P¹)ω.

If μ>0, write Δζ=μ rζ distributionally relative to ω. Testing f=1 gives ∫r dζ=0. Let G be n1's logarithmic kernel and U(x)=μ∫G(x,s)r(s)dζ(s). For every finite p≥1, the logarithmic kernel has uniformly bounded L^p(ω) norms, so the integral triangle inequality shows U∈L^p and bounds its norm by that kernel bound times |μrζ|(P¹). Fubini with smooth tests and ΔG(·,s)=δ_s−1 gives Δ(Uω)=μ rζ because ∫r dζ=0. Therefore ζ−Uω is a finite signed measure annihilating Δ. The already proved μ=0 case makes it Cω. Thus ζ=gω with g=C+U∈L² and Δg=μrg∈L². This step used no regularity theorem for invariant measures or even for arbitrary harmonic distributions.

The energy test is justified spectrally. Let g_N be finite harmonic projections. The equation gives −μ_k g_k=(μrg)_k. Parseval implies ∑μ_k²|g_k|²<∞ and hence ∑μ_k|g_k|²<∞. Testing against the smooth real function g_N gives −∑_{k≤N}μ_k|g_k|²=μ∫r g g_N ω. As g_N→g in L², the right side tends to μ∫r g²ω≥μ min(r)||g||²₂, while the left side is nonpositive. Thus g=0 and ζ=0. Real and imaginary parts also establish the assertion for complex measures if needed. This proves the scalar lemma for all finite signed measures.

Now suppose σ is a finite signed measure on X with ∫L_u h dσ=0 for all smooth real h. Define τ=A(x)^(−1)σ, a finite signed measure, and r(x)=A(x)/b(x)>0. Then ∫[Δ₁h+rΔ₂h]dτ=0. For each y-harmonic e_k define τ_k on the first sphere by ∫f dτ_k=∫f(x)e_k(y)dτ. Testing h=f(x)e_k(y) gives ∫[Δ₁f−μ_k r f]dτ_k=0. The scalar lemma yields τ_0=Cω₁ and τ_k=0 for k>0.

Finite sums of smooth f(x) times y-harmonics are uniformly dense in C(X), by density on the factors and density of finite tensor sums. These identities determine τ=C dW, hence every finite signed annihilator is σ=C A dW. For a probability, 1=C∫Aω₁=Ca, so σ=ν. This covers all Borel probabilities, including singular probabilities, without an absolute-continuity assumption.

The full supporting set is nonempty by the permitted theorem whose antecedents n1 verified. Every member annihilates L_u, and the invariant probability is unique. Consequently Aφ(F)={ν} on the full C(X). ν's full supporting inequality follows from existence and uniqueness; it is not inferred merely from the density ansatz.

Finally, let ρ̃ be nonnegative measurable and integrable, with ∫ρ̃Ω²=1 and dd^c(ρ̃Ω)=0. Integrability relative to dW and Ω² is equivalent because their densities are bounded above and below positively. Multiplication by bounded continuous Ω defines an order-zero current. Set σ̃=ρ̃Ω². For smooth h, ∫L_u h dσ̃=2∫ρ̃Ω∧dd^c h=0. Hence σ̃=ν. Since Ω²=2Ab dW is strictly positive, ρ̃=1/(2ab) almost everywhere. This is uniqueness of the normalized measurable weight as an equivalence class; values on null sets cannot be determined by a current equation.

These arguments are retained in proof.md, section n2. They are ordinary proofs, not conclusions from execution.

notes.summary: Proves all four approximation limits for every fixed-pole smooth residual sequence with uniform tensor convergence, including the actual weighted currents and multiplier measures. The class is nonempty and admits genuinely nonsymmetric sequences.
notes.detailedSummary: For arbitrary smooth mean-zero w_j on all X satisfying Ω_j=η+dd^c w_j>0 and Ω_j→Ω uniformly, u_j=ψ+w_j retains the reference type and F_j→F uniformly. The classical adjoint probabilities μ_j=ρ_jΩ_j² are stationary for operators converging on smooth tests to L_u; n2's uniqueness forces μ_j→ν. Uniform determinant positivity then gives ρ_jdW=(Ω_j²/dW)^(−1)μ_j→ρdW. Testing the weighted currents using uniformly convergent coefficients proves ρ_jΩ_j→Q. No pointwise multiplier control or higher derivative convergence is assumed. Rotation smoothing constructs one sequence, and small mixed-factor smooth perturbations construct nonsymmetric sequences.
notes.text:
Use n1–n2. Let w_j be arbitrary smooth real mean-zero functions on all X with Ω_j=η+dd^c w_j>0 and Ω_j→Ω uniformly as tensors. Then θ+dd^c(ψ+w_j)=λ[D]+Ω_j. Thus u_j=ψ+w_j is genuine θ-psh, has the exact fixed logarithmic pole, and is of type φ for every j. Its extended products are Ω_j and Ω_j².

Put s_j=Ω_j²/dW and s=Ω²/dW=2Ab. Tensor convergence gives s_j→s uniformly. Since s has a positive minimum, all sufficiently late s_j have a uniform positive lower bound. Consequently F_j=log(s_j/(cq)) converges uniformly to log(2Ab/(cq))=F. The actual equation for u_j and the admissible scalar uniqueness theorem give cφ(F_j)=c. The reference antecedents are exactly those proved in n1, and the constructed u_j are genuine solutions in that reference type.

For the classical smooth residual weights impose positivity, dd^c(ρ_jΩ_j)=0, and ∫ρ_jΩ_j²=1. Their existence is the classical smooth positive-form adjoint fact supplied in the input, applied only to smooth strictly positive Ω_j on the compact connected surface. The argument below works for every choice satisfying these equations.

Let μ_j=ρ_jΩ_j², a probability, and L_j h=2Ω_j∧dd^c h/Ω_j². The current equation gives ∫L_j h dμ_j=0. For each fixed smooth h, uniform tensor convergence and the determinant lower bound imply L_j h→L_u h uniformly. Any weak subsequential limit μ of μ_j therefore satisfies ∫L_u h dμ=0 for every smooth h. The complete uniqueness proof in n2 gives μ=ν. Compactness of probabilities on compact X and uniqueness of every subsequential limit prove ρ_jΩ_j²→ν weakly.

The weighted products require an additional argument. As finite measures, exactly ρ_j dW=s_j^(−1)μ_j. Uniform convergence s_j^(−1)→s^(−1) implies, for every continuous f,

∫fρ_j dW=∫(f/s_j)dμ_j→∫(f/s)dν=∫fρ dW.

Thus ρ_jdW→ρdW, and these finite measures have uniformly bounded total masses.

For any smooth test (1,1)-form ξ, define k_j=(Ω_j∧ξ)/dW and k=(Ω∧ξ)/dW. Uniform tensor convergence gives k_j→k uniformly and therefore k_j/s_j→k/s uniformly. Hence

⟨ρ_jΩ_j,ξ⟩=∫(k_j/s_j)dμ_j→∫(k/s)dν=∫ρΩ∧ξ=⟨Q,ξ⟩.

This proves ρ_jΩ_j→Q as currents. It is the coefficient argument that weak convergence of a probability alone cannot provide. Uniform residual tensor convergence and determinant positivity supply the missing control; no pointwise bound or convergence of the conformal multipliers is assumed, and no higher derivatives are used.

The class is nonempty. Lift n1's rotation-smoothed mean-zero w_j⁰ to X. Then Ω_j⁰=A_jω₁+bω₂>0, Ω_j⁰→Ω uniformly, and w_j⁰→w uniformly. To construct a nonsymmetric sequence, choose a smooth mean-zero f(x,y) depending on y, for example the product t_x t_y of standard height functions on the factors. Let κ=min(min A,min b)>0 and choose M with −Mβ≤dd^c f≤Mβ. For nonzero δ_j→0 with |δ_j|M≤κ/2, set w_j=w_j⁰+δ_j f. These functions are smooth on all X, mean zero, and genuinely y-dependent. They converge uniformly to w and satisfy Ω_j≥(κ/2)β>0 and Ω_j→Ω uniformly. Thus the theorem is independent of symmetry within the prescribed class.

This proves all four required limits for every sequence in that class: F_j→F uniformly, ρ_jΩ_j²→ν weakly, ρ_jΩ_j→Q as currents, and ρ_jdW→ρdW as finite measures. The arguments are retained in proof.md, section n3.

notes.summary: Verifies the genuinely nonsmooth example and proves the pole-filling obstruction, including divisor mass 1/5 and a surviving weighted-current divisor. Together with n1–n3, claims complete reconstruction of every frozen target, with restricted approximation independence and all requested scope boundaries.
notes.detailedSummary: For a=1, λ=1/4, q=1, b=2+t and A=1/2+|t|, all antecedents hold, ε=1/2 is admissible, c=1, the residual is continuous uniformly positive and nonsmooth, and ρ=1/(2(2+t)). Exact integrals give MA mass 4, supporting t moment 0 and normalized MA t moment 5/24. In the same background with A=1, decreasing smooth pole-filling potentials have classical adjoint probabilities converging to ((ω₁+λδ_p)/(1+λ))∧ω₂ and weighted raw currents with a positive divisor. These approximations lose the fixed singularity type and have unbounded horizontal tensors, so they lie outside n3. The four notes establish the exact restricted S07 sufficient-condition targets, without asserting arbitrary-potential, degenerate-solution, arbitrary-density, potential-uniqueness or unrestricted approximation results.
notes.text:
Take a=1, λ=1/4, q=1, t=(|Z₀|²−|Z₁|²)/(|Z₀|²+|Z₁|²), b=2+t, and A=H=1/2+|t|. The function t is a smooth nonconstant height in [−1,1], and its distribution under ω₁ is dt/2: r=|z|² gives t=(1−r)/(1+r), with radial area dr/(1+r)²=−dt/2. Thus b is smooth positive nonconstant, with 1≤b≤3. A is continuous with minimum 1/2 and mean 1/2+1/2=1. Consequently m=a=c=1, and F=log(2Ab) satisfies q e^F/(2b)=H exactly. A is nondifferentiable at t=0, so Ω=Aω₁+bω₂ is continuous uniformly positive and nonsmooth. The cusp in log A also makes F nonsmooth; smooth log b cannot cancel it.

All reference and background antecedents follow from n1. Explicitly K=5/4, R=4, and ε=1/2 belongs to (λ/K,1)=(1/5,1), with εK−λ=3/8>0. The reference horizontal residual vanishes on r>4. Its positive finite mass in this example is 2K∫_{t>−3/5}(2+t)dt/2=22/5. The mean-zero continuous w constructed in n1 solves dd^c w=(|t|−1/2)ω₁ and gives the genuine fixed-pole solution. Its normalized weight and full supporting probability are ρ=1/(2(2+t)) and ν=(1/2+|t|)dW by n2; n3 supplies the required approximation class and all its limits.

Oddness gives ∫tAω₁=0. Therefore ∫Ω²=2∫A(2+t)ω₁=4 and ∫t dν=0. Also ∫t²Aω₁=(1/2)(1/3)+1/4=5/12, using ∫t²ω₁=1/3 and ∫|t|³ω₁=1/4. Hence ∫t(Ω²/4)=(1/2)∫tA(2+t)ω₁=5/24. In particular the genuine supporting probability differs from the normalized Monge–Ampère measure.

For the scope obstruction retain the same background with a=1 and instead take H=A=1 and w=0. The factored density is F₀=log(2b), the genuine solution is ψ, and its residual Ω₀=ω₁+bω₂ has scalar c=1, full support dW and residual weight 1/(2b), by n1–n2.

For 0<δ≤1 define ψδ=λ log((|Z₀|²+δ|Z₁|²)/(|Z₀|²+|Z₁|²)). Its numerator is positive on projective space, so it is smooth. As δ decreases to zero it decreases pointwise to ψ, including −∞ on D. Since ψ≤ψδ≤0 and ψ is logarithmically integrable, dominated convergence also gives ψδ→ψ in L¹.

Let ωδ be the smooth Fubini–Study form associated with |Z₀|²+δ|Z₁|². It is the pullback of ω₁ under [Z₀:Z₁]↦[Z₀:√δ Z₁], so it is positive and has integral one. Then dd^c ψδ=λ(ωδ−ω₁), and Γδ:=θ+dd^c ψδ=ω₁+λωδ+bω₂>0. Writing ωδ=kδω₁ gives kδ=δ(1+r)²/(1+δr)². Its mass on every fixed disk r≤R₀ is δR₀/(1+δR₀), tending to zero, hence ωδ→δ_p weakly. Its pullback to X tends to [D]. This also follows distributionally from the preceding L¹ convergence.

The actual classical normalized weight for Γδ is ρδ=1/(2(1+λ)b). Indeed ρδΓδ=(ω₁+λωδ)/(2(1+λ)b)+ω₂/(2(1+λ)) is closed, since its variable horizontal coefficient depends only on x. Its weighted volume is the probability

ρδΓδ²=((ω₁+λωδ)/(1+λ))∧ω₂.

If uniqueness of the classical choice is required, n2's invariant-measure proof applies with horizontal coefficient Bδ=1+λkδ and mean 1+λ. Thus these are precisely the normalized classical adjoints. Their probabilities converge to ((ω₁+λδ_p)/(1+λ))∧ω₂. This assigns D mass λ/(1+λ)=1/5 for λ=1/4, while the genuine full supporting probability dW assigns D mass zero.

The weighted raw currents converge as well. Multiplying ωδ→δ_p by the smooth function b^(−1) yields

ρδΓδ → (1/(2(1+λ)b))ω₁+(1/(2(1+λ)))ω₂+(λ/(2(1+λ)b(p)))[D].

The divisorial component is strictly positive. For b=2+t, p has t=−1 and b(p)=1, so with λ=1/4 its coefficient is 1/10.

These approximations are outside the stipulated class for two precise reasons. Each ψδ is smooth and finite on D, with zero pole coefficient, whereas ψ+w_j retains coefficient λ. The difference ψδ−ψ diverges to +∞ at D and cannot be smooth on all X or bounded. Thus ψδ is not of ordinary type φ. Moreover kδ(p)=1/δ diverges, so its horizontal raw tensor cannot converge uniformly to the positive residual. This pole-filling sequence fails both the fixed-pole and uniform-residual requirements. Its limit does not contradict n3 and expressly prevents an unrestricted approximation claim.
